## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Big Pharma]** **AlphaFold virtual screening identifies novel CLIP1-LTK inhibitors** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43026274/)
  - Structure-based virtual screening leveraging AlphaFold models identified novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the CLIP1-LTK fusion kinase.

- **Genetic analysis refutes PSEN1 loss-of-function as cause of early-onset Alzheimer's disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.13.26367865)
  - Analysis of 45 carriers of predicted loss-of-function (LoF) *PSEN1* stop-gain variants across ADSP, UK Biobank, and BioVU identified no cases of early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), with 17 carriers remaining dementia-free past age 65.
  - Re-analysis of a reported EOAD-associated *PSEN1* p.K109* variant revealed an in-frame 5-amino-acid deletion (p.K109_L113del) caused by a cryptic splice site, demonstrating that altered protein products rather than true null LoF alleles are required to drive EOAD.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Semaglutide accelerates muscle loss in aged mouse models** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.766063)
  - Treatment of 21-month-old high-fat-diet-induced obese mice with daily subcutaneous semaglutide (3 or 30 nmol/kg) for 3 weeks significantly increased lean mass loss compared to vehicle controls.
  - Highlights potential sarcopenia risks associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment in older populations.

- **Gut and urogenital microbiomes modulate clinical response to menopausal hormone therapy** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04789-6)
  - A 6-month prospective study demonstrated that menopausal hormone therapy induces multi-site microbiome remodeling, shifting vaginal microbial composition toward a reproductive-stage profile.
  - Baseline gut and vaginal microbiome profiles predicted rapid symptom remission, offering a potential baseline stratification tool for menopausal care.

- **New approach methodologies advance immunogenicity risk assessment for novel modalities** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01562-9)
  - Perspective outlines the deployment of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), combining computational modeling and human organoid assays, to replace traditional animal models for evaluating immunogenicity in cell and gene therapies.

- **KRAS-targeted cancer vaccines emerge as strategy against pancreatic cancer recurrence** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04772-1)
  - Review highlights recent progress in therapeutic neoantigen and mutant KRAS-targeted vaccines aimed at eradicating minimal residual disease to prevent pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma recurrence.

- **Proteomic exposome mapping connects lifestyle factors to GLP-1 therapy biology** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.07.25327178)
  - The Human Exposomic Architecture of the Proteome (HEAP) framework profiled 2,686 plasma proteins across >50,000 UK Biobank participants, mapping protein signatures associated with 169 lifestyle exposures.
  - Integrated Mendelian randomization and clinical trial datasets from exercise and GLP-1 receptor agonist studies to differentiate causal molecular intermediates from observational disease reporters.

- **Large-scale GWAS identifies 1,717 loci modulating smoking initiation across generations** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.11.26367842)
  - Meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies across nearly 7 million individuals identified 1,717 loci linked to smoking initiation, showing higher SNP-based heritability in females and younger generations across diverse ancestries.

- **Microbiota-derived fecal extracellular vesicles alter gut motility and behavior in autism model** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.754921)
  - Fecal extracellular vesicles (EVs) isolated from patients with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) induced anxiolytic-like behavior, altered social interaction, and accelerated gastrointestinal transit when transferred into mice.
  - ASD EVs disrupted intracellular calcium dynamics and enhanced nitric oxide signaling in enteric neurons via FFAR3-dependent pathways.

- **Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity attenuated by Xiao Chai Hu Decoction via gut-heart axis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43026582/)
  - Preclinical study demonstrated that Xiao Chai Hu Decoction protects against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by modulating *Akkermansia muciniphila* abundance and gut-heart signaling pathways.

- **Neuroimaging meta-analysis identifies shared gray matter volume deficits across psychiatric conditions** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.18.26365862)
  - Voxel-based morphometry meta-analysis of 147 studies (n = 13,041) mapped common gray matter volume reductions in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, ventral anterior cingulate cortex, insula, and superior temporal gyrus across major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and alcohol use disorder.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **First-in-human trial of PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib published with author correction** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43026273/)
  - Author correction issued for the Phase 1 trial evaluating roginolisib, an allosteric, conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor, in patients with advanced solid tumors, including metastatic uveal melanoma.

- **Accelerated TMS alters frontoparietal-subgenual ACC dynamics in major depression** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.12.26367710)
  - 7T resting-state fMRI study of 24 patients with major depression receiving left DLPFC accelerated TMS (aTMS) demonstrated significant longitudinal changes in frontoparietal-subgenual anterior cingulate cortex joint temporal complexity (bMSE-CI interaction p = 0.0188) compared to 15 healthy controls.

- **Real-world trial tracks daily food noise dynamics under weekly GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist therapy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.13.26367932)
  - Prospective study in 237 adults receiving weekly semaglutide or tirzepatide evaluated daily food-related experiences via 24-hour electronic diaries over 6 weeks.
  - Daily food noise prevalence ranged from 4.3% to 23.8%, peaking on injection day (Day 1), declining mid-cycle, and rebounding by Day 7; 76.8% of participants reported food cravings during the observation window.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **Network meta-analysis maps 1-year efficacy and discontinuation trade-offs across obesity drugs** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.13.26367524)
  - Estimand-aligned Bayesian longitudinal network meta-analysis of 178 randomized trials (n = 81,014) evaluated 52-week weight loss, permanent discontinuation rates, and dose titration schedules for obesity pharmacotherapies.
  - Identified major trial evidence gaps, noting that only 78 of 196 randomization units provided complete 1-year longitudinal data.

- **Meta-analysis indicates SGLT2 inhibitors lower cardiovascular risks in stage 5 CKD** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.12.26367903)
  - Meta-analysis of 5 observational cohorts comprising 57,156 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease (28,559 SGLT2 inhibitor users) linked SGLT2 inhibitor treatment to reduced risk of heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.72–0.85) and acute myocardial infarction (HR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.56–0.72).

- **Phase 3 SUCCESS C subanalysis evaluates food intake impact on chemotherapy-induced nausea** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43026373/)
  - Secondary analysis of the randomized Phase 3 SUCCESS C trial evaluated the influence of pre-chemotherapy dietary intake on chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in early-stage breast cancer patients receiving standard regimens.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves obinutuzumab (Gazyva) for primary membranous nephropathy** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-adults-primary-membranous-nephropathy)
  - FDA approved Roche's CD20-directed antibody Gazyva (obinutuzumab) to induce proteinuria remission in adults with primary membranous nephropathy at risk of disease progression.
  - Supported by efficacy data from the Phase 3 MAJESTY study (NCT04629248; n = 142), establishing the first FDA-approved therapeutic specifically indicated for this rare autoimmune kidney disease.

- **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin for muscle-invasive bladder cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-durvalumab-enfortumab-vedotin-ejfv-muscle-invasive-bladder-cancer)
  - FDA approved AstraZeneca's Imfinzi (durvalumab) in combination with Pfizer/Astellas' Padcev (enfortumab vedotin-ejfv) as neoadjuvant therapy, followed by adjuvant single-agent durvalumab post-cystectomy, for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) ineligible for or refusing cisplatin.
  - Approval was granted based on event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) improvements in the randomized Phase 3 VOLGA trial (NCT04960709; n = 695).

- **[Big Pharma]** **Novo Nordisk files etavopivat regulatory submission for sickle cell disease** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-etavopivat-flagship-gates-ascidian-immuneering-neurosterix/874120/)
  - Novo Nordisk submitted a regulatory application for etavopivat, an oral pyruvate kinase R (PKR) activator acquired through its $1.1 billion purchase of Forma Therapeutics, targeting sickle cell disease.

- **FDA updates guidance on master protocols and clinical food-effect studies** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidances-drugs/guidance-recap-podcast-master-protocols-drug-and-biological-product-development)
  - FDA issued a revised draft guidance titled *Master Protocols for Drug and Biological Product Development*, refining statistical standards and structural guidelines for basket, umbrella, and platform trials.
  - Published final guidance on *Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs*, detailing clinical pharmacology design expectations for oral drug filings.

- **FDA issues compliance deadline for CARES Act annual drug reporting** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-shortages/coronavirus-aid-relief-and-economic-security-act-cares-act-drug-shortage-mitigation-efforts)
  - FDA reminded registered drug manufacturers that noncompliant entities failing to submit calendar year 2025 drug production volumes under section 510(j)(3) of the FD&C Act by December 31, 2026, will be publicly listed in early 2027.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **Boston Scientific marketing practices for Watchman implant face clinical scrutiny** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/investigation-boston-scientific-watchman-cardiac-implant-marketing-science/)
  - A investigative report raised questions regarding whether Boston Scientific's commercial promotion of the Watchman left atrial appendage closure device outpaced published clinical trial evidence to expand clinical adoption.

- **Industry commentary warns against oversimplified AI timelines in drug discovery** [Science Blogs](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/stop-it-just-stop-it)
  - Clinical discovery commentary refutes public statements by tech executives predicting the total elimination of major diseases like cancer and Alzheimer's within a decade via AI, emphasizing intractable biological complexity and historical translational failure rates.

## Public Health & Policy

- **HHS commits $4.9 million to ibogaine research for PTSD and addiction** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/biotech-news-hhs-funding-for-research-into-ibogaine-for-ptsd/)
  - The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced up to $4.9 million in federal grant funding to support clinical research into ibogaine for treating post-traumatic stress disorder and substance use disorders.

- **ASAM issues first clinical management guidance for medetomidine withdrawal** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/medetomidine-withdrawal-asam-new-treatment-guidance/)
  - The American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) published the first national guidance establishing clinical protocols to identify and treat acute withdrawal caused by medetomidine, an alpha-2 agonist increasingly detected in illicit drug markets.

- **Federal enforcement of Medicaid work requirements delayed to July 2027** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/13/medicaid-work-requirements-implementation-delayed-six-months/)
  - Implementation and enforcement of revised Medicaid work mandate regulations have been officially postponed for six months, establishing a new effective date of July 1, 2027.

- **Global Burden of Disease study quantifies shifting childhood respiratory mortality patterns** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.01.26361937)
  - Analysis of GBD 2023 data across 29 cause nodes (26 lower respiratory infection etiologies, tuberculosis, COVID-19, and pertussis) tracked changing etiology distribution and geographic concentration of pediatric mortality from 1990 to 2023.

- **Nationwide study documents 74% increase in unruptured intracranial aneurysm incidence** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.12.26367153)
  - Longitudinal analysis of 8,681 patients in the Swedish National Patient Register (2000–2020) demonstrated an increase in age-standardized unruptured intracranial aneurysm incidence from 4.6 per 100,000 in 2000 to 7.99 per 100,000 in 2019.

- Biology & Health
    - [Weird Heart Disease Effect of Cheese](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/qCPfJ0emUJE) -- Physionic
        - A randomized trial demonstrated that full-fat cheese lowered LDL cholesterol more than reduced-fat cheese supplemented with butter, despite matching calories, protein, and saturated fat levels.
        - Research indicates higher fecal fat excretion in individuals consuming cheese compared to butter, suggesting that calcium, proteins, and the structural "cheese matrix" reduce fat absorption during digestion.
        - Results suggest that a food's total saturated-fat content does not fully predict its cardiovascular or cholesterol effects.
        - While cheese can be included in a heart-healthy diet, potential health benefits appear to level off at approximately 50 grams per day.
    - [Healthcare Investors, Prior Authorization & Startup Life | HealthTech #DadJokes](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Oo3jOBZCXRM) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Hosts Alex Koshykov and Sergei Polevikov present a segment of "HealthTech Dad Jokes" on the Digital Health Inside Out channel.
        - The humor focuses on healthcare venture capital investors, startup scaling, U.S. healthcare prior authorization, and the life cycle of digital health founders.
        - Content touches on common digital health startup experiences, such as fundraising hurdles, pilot fatigue, and regulatory/administrative friction.
    - [Your Startup Idea Doesn't Matter](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/i0h74vjzVlc) -- Health2Tech
        - Bret Waters states that the initial idea behind a startup is rarely the primary factor determining its ultimate success.
        - Realizing startup success depends primarily on sustained execution over several years rather than the original concept.
        - Key factors driving successful execution include continuously listening to market feedback and adapting the business along the way.
- To watch
    - [How Absolute Zero Was Discovered](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cy0lixk3aVw) -- Abide By Reason
